Bug report:
Title: ArrayUtils.add(T[] array, T element) can create unexpected ClassCastException

ArrayUtils.add(T[] array, T element) can create an unexpected ClassCastException.

For example, the following code compiles without a warning:

{code}
String[] sa = ArrayUtils.add(stringArray, aString);
{code}

and works fine, provided at least one of the parameters is non-null. However, if both parameters are null, the add() method returns an Object[] array, hence the Exception.

If both parameters are null, it's not possible to determine the correct array type to return, so it seems to me this should be disallowed.

I think the method ought to be changed to throw IllegalParameterException when both parameters are null.

input.issue_gist: ArrayUtils.add(T[] array, T element) returns an Object[] when both the array and element are null, since the component type can't be determined. Callers who assign the result to a typed array like String[] get an unexpected ClassCastException at runtime, with no compile-time warning.

concrete_examples.expected: The call should not return an Object[]. The reporter proposes throwing an IllegalArgumentException, since the array type can't be determined when both arguments are null.
concrete_examples.actual: add() returns an Object[] containing a single null. Assigning it to String[] throws ClassCastException.

concrete_examples.input: String[] stringArray = null; String aString = null; String[] sa = ArrayUtils.add(stringArray, aString);
concrete_examples.expected: A clear, deliberate failure (IllegalArgumentException) or a correctly typed result, instead of a ClassCastException.

concrete_examples.actual: Works correctly. The array type is taken from the non-null array, so no bug here.
